To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) Stem cell fate can be explained by a self-organizing system, (2) Asymmetric stem cell division is neither necessary, nor sufficient to explain stem cell fate heterogeneity, and (3) Stem cell heterogeneity can be understood as the result of reversible changes in cell fate potentials, induced by cell-cell and cell-environment interactions.
Stem cell heterogeneity is not necessarily the result of asymmetry of cell divisions, but can also be the result of reversible expression of stem cell potential.
Stem cell heterogeneity can be generated through a combination of reversible expression of stem cell potential and asymmetric cell division.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question of whether the concept of asymmetric stem cell fate is a prerequisite to understand the observed heterogeneity of HSC fate or whether it can alternatively be explained in a self-organizing way.
the fundamental question regarding the nature of the tissue stem cells.
the development of mathematical models for the self-organization of tissue-specific stem cell systems.
